entities.summary:
Vijayadashami, also known as Dussehra, is a significant event in South Asian history, commemorating the triumph of good over evil as depicted in the Hindu epic, the Ramayana. This annual festival marks the culmination of the nine-day Navaratri celebrations, which honor the divine feminine in various forms.


It is observed on the tenth day after the full moon in the month of Ashwin, typically in September or October. The festivities involve the symbolic destruction of the effigy of Ravana, the demon king from the Ramayana, marking the victory of Lord Rama and his brother Lakshmana over the evil forces.


The event has cultural and spiritual significance, symbolizing the eternal struggle between good and evil. The legacy of Vijayadashami can be seen in the various forms of art, music, and dance that are created to commemorate this occasion, such as the traditional folk dances of the Garba and Dandiya Raas. The event also has a deep impact on the spiritual lives of millions of people, inspiring them to reflect on the importance of virtues like courage, wisdom, and devotion.


One of the most poignant aspects of this festival is its emphasis on the triumph of good over evil, serving as a powerful reminder of the enduring values of righteousness and justice.
